page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores operating at 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 672.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 3686 GB of local SSD storage. This high memory-to-vCPU ratio positions the server in the memory-optimized category, designed for memory-intensive workloads that also require high-capacity local temporary storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. While single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score, fall in the average range, multi-threaded execution is highly efficient. The server achieved strong results in the stress-ng multi-core CPU test, Geekbench multi-core score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including both small-block cached and large-block uncached read/write operations, consistently rank in the top 25%. Notably, the Passmark CPU encryption test reached top-tier status, placing in the top 10%, while database operations and Redis SET operations demonstrated strong throughput.

The qualitative cost profile of the E96ds_v5 reflects its high resource density, offering a balanced tradeoff between massive memory capacity and substantial local SSD storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable execution, though workloads relying heavily on single-threaded performance may find the average single-core speeds a limiting factor compared to newer high-frequency processors. Given these characteristics, the server is suited for large-scale database deployments, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data warehousing, and complex multi-threaded enterprise applications.
